item.title: Britain Arms Ukraine Against Russia’s Drone Swarms
item.description: The UK has delivered more than 1,000 air defence missiles and over 250,000 rounds of air defence ammunition to Ukraine thus far in 2025. The post Britain Arms Ukraine Against Russia’s Drone Swarms appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The Dark Eagle Hypersonic Missile Will Pierce China’s A2/AD Bubble
item.description: The Dark Eagle missile will allow the US Army to bypass current anti-access/area denial (A2/AD) umbrellas with ease. The post The Dark Eagle Hypersonic Missile Will Pierce China’s A2/AD Bubble appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Trump’s “Western Hemisphere Command” Is Just the Start of His New Plans
item.description: Trump’s national security strategy outlines a broad rethinking of American defense priorities—starting from the Western Hemisphere and branching outward. The post Trump’s “Western Hemisphere Command” Is Just the Start of His New Plans appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: On General Patton’s Death Anniversary, We Remember How He Inspires Even Today
item.description: Patton was not an ideal commander. But his fighting spirit was second to none—and continues to inspire military leaders in the United States today. The post On General Patton’s Death Anniversary, We Remember How He Inspires Even Today appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: How a British Magician (May Have) Outsmarted the Nazis in World War II
item.description: The legend of Jasper Maskelyne, a British stage magician who helped hide Allied military installations during World War II, has likely been embellished beyond his actual accomplishments. The post How a British Magician (May Have) Outsmarted the Nazis in World War II appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: What Is the US Navy’s “Advanced Arresting Gear”—and Why Is It So Controversial?
item.description: The Ford-class aircraft carrier’s AAG system is far better than the old steam-based hydraulic catapults—but the Navy has struggled with technical issues in its implementation. item.title: Here’s How a US Attack on Venezuela Might Play Out
item.description: An actual ground invasion of Venezuela is still unlikely—but the United States could launch a military campaign from the air, as it did in Libya in 2011. The post Here’s How a US Attack on Venezuela Might Play Out appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why Do Fifth-Gen Fighter Jets Use “Thrust Vectoring”?
item.description: Thrust vectoring—essentially redirecting the plane’s exhaust flow—allows modern fighters to quickly change direction, giving them an edge in close combat. The post Why Do Fifth-Gen Fighter Jets Use “Thrust Vectoring”? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Did China Get Germany’s Boxer Armored Vehicle from Ukraine?
item.description: It seems unlikely that China could so accurately copy a German armored vehicle from schematics alone. Could it have obtained a live one from the battlefield in Ukraine? The post Did China Get Germany’s Boxer Armored Vehicle from Ukraine? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The Bayraktar Akinci UAV Is Cementing Turkey’s Drone Superpower Status
item.description: The Akinci can fly at an altitude of up to 40,000 feet and is making waves on the international arms export market. The post The Bayraktar Akinci UAV Is Cementing Turkey’s Drone Superpower Status appeared first on The National Interest.
